title: Does shifting preserve or move values?
hook: Compare filtering before and after a shift.

knows: A network has weights that training nudges to lower a loss.
doesNotKnow: Distinguish output translation from invariance and test boundary/stride conditions.

objective: Distinguish output translation from invariance and test boundary/stride conditions.
misconception: A convolution output stays unchanged for every input shift.

claims.text: Centered cross-correlation filter[1,2,1] on six cells. Circular boundary and stride1 are the primary convention; shift is circular right-one.
claims.source: src/demos/ai/ai-translation-equivariance/Demo.tsx#picture#filter; src/demos/ai/ai-translation-equivariance/model.ts + model.test.mjs finite author implementation reproduction; https://d2l.ai/chapter_convolutional-neural-networks/why-conv.html §7.1 and https://d2l.ai/chapter_convolutional-neural-networks/padding-and-strides.html §7.3 — bodies opened 2026-10-19; equivariance and padding/stride background. Finite circular/zero-filled operators and arrays are local definitions.

claims.text: Input[1,0,0,0,0,0] filters to[2,1,0,0,0,1]. Shift then filter and filter then shift both give[1,2,1,0,0,0]. Values move, not remain unchanged.

claims.text: Circular stride2 samples indices0,2,4. Old[2,0,0]; input shift1 gives[1,1,0], unlike shifted old[0,2,0]. Input shift2 gives[0,2,0], matching one output shift.

claims.text: Zero-padded edge impulse[0,0,0,0,0,1] filters to[0,0,0,0,1,2]. Cropped input right shift loses it and filters to all0; shifted old output[0,0,0,0,0,1] differs.
